detail_statements: The solar system may have formed from a large nebula after a nearby star exploded.
A supernova is an explosion of a big star.
The young planets eventually became the eight planets listed in the source.
Mercury is one of the planets in the solar system.
Venus is one of the planets in the solar system.
Earth is one of the planets in the solar system.
Mars is one of the planets in the solar system.
Jupiter is one of the planets in the solar system.
Saturn is one of the planets in the solar system.
Uranus is one of the planets in the solar system.
Neptune is one of the planets in the solar system.
A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling.
A supernova has enough energy to make gas and dust in nearby nebulae start spinning.
The swirling caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.
The spinning caused material in the nebula to fall into its center.
Collisions among gas and dust formed little pieces of metal and rock.
Many collisions over a long time formed the eight planets.
Planet formation produced the eight planets.
The planets move around the Sun.

evidence.quote: We currently think that our solar system formed from a large nebula, perhaps after the explosion of a nearby star.
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: Some big stars can explode, something called a supernova

evidence.quote: These were young planets, and eventually, over a long time and through many, many collisions, our eight planets were formed – Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: Some big stars can explode, something called a supernova, and that explosion has enough energy to make the gas and dust in nearby nebulae start swirling and spinning about.
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: As this happened, it caused a lot of the material in the nebula to fall into its center, and that’s where the Sun started forming.
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: Meanwhile, the rest of the gas and dust in the nebula began colliding and sticking together, making little pieces of metal and rock.
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: That’s why we see the planets moving around the Sun the way that they do today!
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?

evidence.quote: We call the pattern that the planets make when they go around the Sun an “orbit.”
evidence.source_title: How did our Solar System form?
